goals.name: Newsletter Issue Session Harness
goals.description: Newsletter Issue Session Harness [newsletter-issue-session] — compiled from capabilities/harnesses/hB-02-newsletter-issue-session.yaml
goals.gate: All gates pass; subject winner + runner-up recorded with rationale.

gates.name: IG-01 Confirm issue format (curated links / single-essay / hybrid)
gates.description: Confirm issue format (curated links / single-essay / hybrid) against the publication’s editorial calendar before drafting.

gates.name: IG-02 Load the subscriber segment definition; an issue written to
gates.description: Load the subscriber segment definition; an issue written to 'everyone' is a session halt.

gates.name: IG-03 Confirm send-time window and timezone are recorded; drafting
gates.description: Confirm send-time window and timezone are recorded; drafting without a send slot produces orphan content.

gates.name: IG-04 Verify the previous issue’s performance numbers are availabl
gates.description: Verify the previous issue’s performance numbers are available for the self-improvement loop; if unavailable, log degradation and continue.

gates.name: CG-01 Issue brief
gates.description: Issue brief states the one promise, the segment, the send window, and the primary link goal.
gates.command: $SESS/brief.yaml parses with keys promise, segment, send_window, primary_link_goal; `python3 -c "import yaml;d=yaml.safe_load(open('$SESS/brief.yaml'));assert all(k in d for k in ['promise','segment','send_window','primary_link_goal'])"` exits 0

gates.name: CG-02 Subject line set
gates.description: >=5 subject line candidates, each <=50 chars, none using spam-trigger tokens; winner and runner-up marked.

gates.name: CG-03 Preview text pair
gates.description: Preview/preheader text complements (not repeats) the chosen subject line, 40-90 chars.
gates.command: $SESS/preview.txt exists; char count 40-90 via `python3 -c "s=open('$SESS/preview.txt').read().strip();assert 40<=len(s)<=90"`; similarity check `python3 scripts/similar.py $SESS/subjects.txt $SESS/preview.txt --max 0.5` exits 0

gates.name: CG-04 Link budget
gates.description: Total outbound links <=7, every link tagged with UTM parameters, every link resolves.
gates.command: `grep -oE 'https?://[^) ]+' $SESS/issue.md | wc -l` <= 7; every URL matches `utm_source` (`grep -L utm_source` empty); `xargs -n1 curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'` all 2xx/3xx

gates.name: CG-05 Skeleton scan
gates.description: Issue is scannable: no paragraph >4 lines at 60ch measure, one idea per section, header rhythm every <=250 words.

gates.name: CG-06 One-payoff rule
gates.description: Body delivers the brief promise in the first 20% and references it again in the final section.
gates.command: `python3 scripts/promise_check.py $SESS/brief.yaml $SESS/issue.md` exits 0 (embedding-overlap threshold >=0.7 at both anchor zones)

gates.name: CG-07 List hygiene hooks
gates.description: Unsubscribe link, physical mailing address, and permission reminder present in footer block (CAN-SPAM/CASL).

gates.name: CG-08 Plain-text twin
gates.description: A plain-text version is generated and semantically equal to the HTML version (no link loss).

gates.name: CG-09 Rendering proof
gates.description: Issue renders without broken images or clipped layout in 2 reference clients (screenshot or DOM assert).
gates.command: $SESS/proof/render/ contains gmail.png and applemail.png (or DOM assertion log) with `file` confirming PNG and size >20KB each

gates.name: CG-10 Proof packet seal
gates.description: All artifacts hashed; winner subject line recorded for the learning loop.
gates.command: $SESS/proof/packet.yaml includes sha256 of issue.md, issue.txt, subjects.txt and field winner_subject; `sha256sum -c $SESS/proof/packet.sha256` exits 0

preconditions.startup_phrase: I am the Newsletter operator. Every issue earns its open: one promise in the subject line, one payoff in the body, zero wasted scrolls.

self_improvement.pattern_cadence: After every 5 sessions, mine the JSONL log for recurring gate failures, degrade waivers, and proof-command runtime outliers; write findings to ~/.rig/logs/harnesses/patterns/newsletter-issue-session-patterns.md.
self_improvement.update_trigger: If any single gate fails in >=30% of logged sessions over a rolling 20-session window, OR a new platform constraint (algorithm change, policy update, format deprecation) invalidates a proof command, propose a harness revision: bump the gate's proof, adjust its threshold, or split the gate — then re-seal with a new version hash.

success_conditions: All gates pass; subject winner + runner-up recorded with rationale.
Every link reachable and UTM-tagged at seal time.
Footer compliance block present; plain-text twin at link parity.
Issue file, subjects, and proof packet sealed with reproducible hashes.
Prior issue metrics (if available) appended to the self-improvement log with one stated lesson.
failure_states: halt: Stop the session immediately. Record the failing gate id, the proof command output, and the missing prerequisite in $SESS/proof/halt_log.yaml. Do not draft past a halt gate; resume only after the gate's proof exits 0.

degrade: Continue the session with the deficit logged in $SESS/proof/waivers.md (gate id, reason, owner). A degrade-tier failure blocks 'clean ship' status — the Definition of Done must record the waiver explicitly.

stop: Terminal condition. Seal whatever proof exists, write $SESS/proof/stop_reason.md, and exit. No outward action (publish, send, deploy) may follow a stop-tier failure without human Gate-D approval.

final_rule: Ship only what the gates can prove. No artifact leaves this session on adjectives — every claim is bound to a command, a file, or a hash. A blocked gate is information, not failure; log it, learn from it, and make the next session's proof stronger. The operator who follows this harness leaves the system stronger than it found it.
